message.content: {"summary":"You submitted an outstanding, professional engineering report that met all rubric requirements to the highest standard. Your mission concept, technical justifications, orbital mechanics calculations, and software verification were exceptionally detailed, cohesive, and clearly documented.","next_steps":["Consider conducting sensitivity analyses on drag-sail deployment reliability to further robustify your end-of-life plan.","Develop the secondary payload or Falcon 9 fallback operational profile to mitigate primary launch vehicle uncertainty.","Explore multi-ground-station networks to evaluate whether downlink latency could be reduced during peak reef-monitoring seasons."],"criteria":{"C1":"You achieved the Accomplished level by clearly establishing the ZYZZsat mission rationale, defining user roles (AIMS and stakeholders), and thoroughly justifying your single-satellite architecture in Section 1. To maintain this high standard, continue supporting user operational requirements with direct quantitative data needs.","C2":"You reached the Accomplished level through exceptional technical rigour in Section 2. You supported your launch vehicle selection, analytical J2 orbital hand calculations, STK modelling, and passive deorbit drag-sail strategy with clear evidence and verification. For future work, consider modelling stochastic atmospheric drag variations during deorbit.","C3":"You achieved Accomplished in Section 3 by providing a concise synthesis of mission objectives alongside an honest, critical appraisal of key design limitations (such as Vega C flight heritage). To build on this, include high-level cost or schedule risk mitigations in future work.","C4":"Your presentation reached the Accomplished level through a clear engineering layout, a concise executive summary, consistent tabular and graphical presentation, immaculate referencing, and complete STK model documentation in Appendix A. Continue using this professional formatting standard for future engineering deliverables."}}
